title: A new fine-scale Berry-Esseen-type Gumbel-limit theorem for multivariate maxima
summary: For $d \geq 2$ and i.i.d. $d$-dimensional observations $\mathbf{X}^{(1)}, \mathbf{X}^{(2)}, \ldots$ with independent Exponential$(1)$ coordinates, let $\varphi_n$ denote the minimum $\ell^1$-norm among the maxima of $\{\mathbf{X}^{(1)}, \ldots, \mathbf{X}^{(n)}\}$. (A _maximum_ from this set is an observation $\mathbf{X}^{(k)}$ with $1 \leq k \leq n$ such that $\mathbf{X}^{(k)} \not\prec \mathbf{X}^{(i)}$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$, where $\mathbf{x} \prec \mathbf{y}$ means that $x_j < y_j$ for $1 \leq j \leq d$.) Key roles in the study of multivariate Pareto records are played by $\varphi_n$…
